nodes.content: Design incremental link-time optimization that safely reuses optimized code despite changing cross-module symbol resolution and optimization dependencies.
requirements: Preserve clean-build semantics across weak-symbol replacement, visibility changes, and cross-module function edits.
For single-function edits, median rebuild time ≤50% of clean LTO, with ≤3% executable runtime regression.

nodes.content: Cache optimized functions with dependency manifests tracking inlined bodies, imported summaries, symbol bindings, and visibility; rebuild the affected closure.
Which recorded dependencies ensure cached functions are invalidated when weak-symbol replacements or visibility changes alter cross-module resolution?
Resolver fingerprints covering candidate definitions, prevailing bindings, and visibility will yield zero stale reuses across weak-symbol and visibility mutations.
Implement resolver fingerprints and dependency-closure invalidation; test weak/visibility mutations and cross-module edits against clean builds, rebuild and runtime budgets.
Run ResolverFlip-200 weak-replacement and visibility-flip cases; compare prevailing bindings and optimized-function hashes with deterministic clean LTO.
ResolverFlip-200 matched clean-LTO bindings and optimized-function hashes in all 200 cases, with zero stale cache reuses.
Adopt resolver fingerprints for invalidation because ResolverFlip-200 found no binding mismatches or stale cache reuses.
Benchmark the adopted fingerprint-backed cache on EditLTO-100 cross-module function edits, measuring rebuild-time ratio, runtime delta, and clean-build equivalence.
EditLTO-100 report records per-edit rebuild ratios, executable runtime deltas, and clean-build equivalence checks for fingerprint-backed reuse.
What dependency granularity keeps cross-module function edits from invalidating excessive cached code while preserving clean-build equivalence?
Compare function-level versus module-level dependency manifests on EditLTO-100, measuring invalidation counts, clean-build hash matches, rebuild ratios, and runtime deltas.
EditLTO-100: function-level manifests produced six clean-build hash mismatches from unimported callee-summary edits; module-level invalidation produced none.
Augment resolver-fingerprinted function caches with epochs for all consulted callee summaries, including nonimported candidates, and invalidate affected partitions.
Instrument summary reads, persist consulted-callee epochs, invalidate dependent partitions, then rerun EditLTO-100 and ResolverFlip-200 against clean LTO.
Use the EditLTO-100 report’s failing edits to instrument nonimported callee-summary reads, persist epochs, and rerun clean-build and timing comparisons.
EpochManifest-v2 records consulted imported and nonimported summary epochs per optimization partition and invalidates partitions when any recorded epoch changes.
Rerun EditLTO-100 and ResolverFlip-200 using EpochManifest-v2; compare hashes with clean LTO, median rebuild ratio, and runtime regression.
EpochManifest-v2 matched clean-LTO hashes in EditLTO-100 and ResolverFlip-200; median rebuild was 43% of clean LTO, worst runtime regression 1.8%.
Does EpochManifest-v2 stay below 50% of clean-LTO rebuild time on 500,000-function links with dense summary dependencies?
On 500,000-function links, EpochManifest-v2 will retain median rebuild time below 50% of clean LTO despite dense summary dependencies.
Benchmark EpochManifest-v2 on DenseLink-500K with 100 single-function edits and 40 cross-module summary readers per function; measure median rebuild/clean-LTO ratio.
DenseLink-500K median rebuild reached 68% of clean LTO across 100 edits, exceeding the hypothesized 50% threshold.
Profile DenseLink-500K’s 100 edits, attributing the 68% rebuild ratio to summary-epoch invalidation fanout, repartitioning, and code generation.
Profiling attributed 25 percentage points to eviction-amplified summary fanout and recompilation; pinned-cache reruns reached 43% of clean LTO.
Adopt pinned-cache mode for DenseLink-500K: eviction raised median rebuild time from 43% to 68% of clean LTO.
Use cost-aware pinning of high-fanout EpochManifest-v2 partitions in a content-addressed cache to reduce eviction-driven recompilation.
Implement 16-GiB cost-and-fanout pinning; rerun DenseLink-500K, EditLTO-100, and ResolverFlip-200 for rebuild, runtime, and clean-build equivalence.
Implement 16-GiB cost-and-fanout pinning for content-addressed EpochManifest-v2 partitions, retaining fingerprint and epoch checks before reuse.
PinCache-16G adds a 16-GiB cost-and-fanout eviction policy while retaining resolver-fingerprint and summary-epoch validation on cache hits.
Run PinCache-16G on DenseLink-500K, EditLTO-100, and ResolverFlip-200; check clean-build hashes, median rebuild ratios, and executable runtime deltas.
DenseLink-500K: PinCache-16G median rebuild rose to 71% of clean LTO versus 68% unpinned, despite matching clean-build hashes.
Which partitions should PinCache-16G prioritize to approach unrestricted pinning’s 43% rebuild ratio on DenseLink-500K?
Profile DenseLink-500K evictions; compare 16-GiB fanout, compile-cost, and edit-local-reuse pinning against PinCache-16G by median rebuild ratio.
DenseLink-500K: high-fanout pinning of expensive partitions cut median rebuild to 48% of clean LTO versus PinCache-16G’s 71%.
Ranking pins by edit-weighted recompilation cost should lower DenseLink-500K median rebuild below 45% of clean LTO within 16 GiB.
Train edit-weighted pin scores on 50 DenseLink-500K edits; measure held-out median rebuild ratio under 16 GiB against the 48% baseline.
On 50 held-out DenseLink-500K edits, edit-weighted pinning achieved 44% median rebuild time versus the 48% baseline within 16 GiB.
Stress-test edit-weighted pinning on 100 new DenseLink-500K edits targeting previously unseen functions; compare median rebuild against 45%.
On 100 unseen-function DenseLink-500K edits, edit-weighted pinning reached 57% median rebuild time, missing the hypothesized 45% threshold.
Restrict edit-weighted pinning to recurring edit patterns; its 44% held-out rebuild ratio rose to 57% on unseen functions.
Combining edit-weighted pins with high-fanout fallback should keep both recurring and unseen-function DenseLink-500K median rebuilds below 50% within 16 GiB.
Reserve 8 GiB for high-fanout partitions, rank remaining pins by edit-weighted cost, and retest recurring and unseen DenseLink-500K edits.
Benchmark the 8-GiB high-fanout reserve plus 8-GiB edit-weighted pins on recurring and unseen DenseLink-500K edits.
With the 16-GiB hybrid reserve, DenseLink-500K median rebuilds were 46% for recurring edits and 49% for unseen-function edits.
Rerun 100 unseen-function DenseLink-500K edits after reshuffling summary-reader fanout; compare hybrid pinning’s median rebuild ratio with 50%.
After summary-reader fanout reshuffling, hybrid pinning’s unseen-function median rebuild reached 54% of clean LTO, exceeding its 50% target.
Limit hybrid pinning to stable fanout workloads: rebuilds met 50% initially but reached 54% after fanout reshuffling.
Refreshing pin priorities after summary-fanout changes should bring reshuffled DenseLink-500K unseen-edit median rebuilds below 50% within 16 GiB.
On reshuffled DenseLink-500K, refresh hybrid pin priorities using current summary fanout; compare unseen-edit median rebuilds against unrefreshed 54%.
Refreshing hybrid pin priorities reduced reshuffled DenseLink-500K unseen-edit median rebuilds from 54% to 48% of clean LTO within 16 GiB.
Repeat refreshed-priority pinning across five independent DenseLink-500K fanout reshuffles; measure per-reshuffle unseen-edit median rebuild ratios.
Across five new DenseLink-500K reshuffles, refreshed pinning yielded unseen-edit median rebuilds of 47%, 49%, 52%, 54%, and 56%.
Gate hybrid pinning on stable fanout; refreshing helps some reshuffles, but three of five still exceed the 50% rebuild budget.
Record per-partition summary queries and answers; invalidate only on changed answers, preserving resolver checks and conservatively invalidating untracked reads.
Instrument summary-query answers with conservative fallback; benchmark answer-delta invalidation on DenseLink-500K reshuffles for clean-build hashes and rebuild/runtime budgets.
Use the EditLTO-100 report’s six mismatch cases to instrument summary-query answers, then test answer-delta invalidation on DenseLink-500K reshuffles.
AnswerTrace-v1 stores each partition’s summary-query key, returned optimization attributes, and resolver fingerprint; uninstrumented queries force conservative invalidation.
Test AnswerTrace-v1 across five DenseLink-500K reshuffles, EditLTO-100, and ResolverFlip-200; compare clean-build hashes, rebuild ratios, and runtime.
AnswerTrace-v1 matched clean-build hashes across all suites; five reshuffled DenseLink-500K medians were 42–47%, with worst runtime regression 1.7%.
Adopt AnswerTrace-v1 with conservative fallback: clean-build hashes matched, reshuffled rebuild medians stayed 42–47%, and worst runtime regression was 1.7%.
Use snapshot-isolated optimization certificates to validate symbol bindings and summary answers before atomically linking cached code.
How can concurrent object-file updates be prevented from mixing symbol bindings and summary answers from different link snapshots?
Snapshot-versioned certificates and commit-time validation will prevent mixed-generation executables during concurrent weak-symbol and callee-summary updates.
Using AnswerTrace-v1 certificates, race 1,000 concurrent weak-symbol and callee-summary updates; verify each executable matches one clean-build snapshot.
Across 1,000 concurrent-update races, every executable matched one clean-build snapshot; commit validation retried 37 conflicting links.
Adopt snapshot-versioned certificates and atomic commit validation; all 1,000 raced links matched a clean-build snapshot.
Integrate adopted snapshot certificates with AnswerTrace-v1; rerun edit, resolution, and concurrent-update suites against clean builds and performance budgets.
Integrate AnswerTrace-v1 certificates with EpochManifest-v2 fallback epochs; run EditLTO-100, ResolverFlip-200, and concurrent-update races against clean LTO.
SnapshotLTO-v1 integrates AnswerTrace-v1 certificates, EpochManifest-v2 fallback epochs, and atomic commit validation, with clean-build and performance test reports.
Benchmark SnapshotLTO-v1 on EditLTO-100, ResolverFlip-200, five DenseLink-500K reshuffles, and 1,000 concurrent races; compare clean-build hashes and performance.
SnapshotLTO-v1 matched clean-build snapshots across all suites and 1,000 races; DenseLink-500K rebuild medians were 44–49%, worst runtime regression 2.1%.
Ship SnapshotLTO-v1: epoch and answer-trace baselines plus snapshot-race equivalence support 44–49% median rebuilds and 2.1% worst runtime regression.
